text: Traditional spoken dialogue systems struggle to feel natural because they rely on cascaded pipelines that introduce several seconds of latency between interactions. [S1] They lose non‑linguistic information such as emotion or non‑speech sounds because text is the intermediate modality. [S1] The pipeline also separates ASR and TTS, so the system must re‑transcribe the user’s speech, further degrading naturalness. [S2]

text: Inner Monologue is a method that generates text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, enabling a single model to produce aligned text and speech representations. [S3] It decomposes speech into a chain of text, semantic and acoustic tokens and predicts this structured sequence hierarchically. [S4] By inserting a delay between the text and audio streams, the model can decide whether to generate audio conditioned on text or text conditioned on audio. [S2] Setting audio ahead of text yields a streaming ASR model that samples only text tokens while using ground‑truth audio, providing precise word‑level alignment. [S2] Conversely, delaying text ahead of audio turns the model into a streaming TTS system, where the content of the audio is dictated by the sampled text. [S2] The same delay hyper‑parameter switches between ASR and TTS without changing the loss, architecture, or training data, demonstrating Inner Monologue’s flexibility. [S2]
